swebench_scaled_no_offload.description: Scaled SWE-Bench-style agent traces without KV offload; paper reports up to roughly 2x average response-time reduction over vanilla vLLM.
swebench_scaled_no_offload.source_note: Paper Section 6.2 states up to roughly 2x average response-time reduction for Llama-3.1-8B end-to-end experiments; exact figure values are image-only in the markdown.

avg_completion_time_s.description: Mean end-to-end program completion time; lower values measure the paper's headline delay reduction goal.

p90_completion_time_s.description: Tail end-to-end completion time; lower values catch methods that improve the mean while leaving slow programs behind.

p95_completion_time_s.description: 95th-percentile end-to-end completion time; lower values measure the paper's tail-latency claim from Figure 10.

avg_queue_wait_s.description: Average per-request queue waiting time; lower values directly probe the scheduling-bubble mechanism targeted by the paper.

throughput_jobs_per_s.description: Completed agent programs per second; higher values measure the paper's throughput benefit without using wall-clock benchmarking.

cache_hit_rate.description: Fraction of reusable cross-turn KV cache accesses served from retained cache; higher values indicate useful continuity preservation.

peak_pinned_memory_fraction.description: Peak fraction of capacity occupied by pinned KV cache; lower values penalize over-pinning shortcuts that create memory pressure.

expired_pin_fraction.description: Fraction of TTL decisions that expired before reuse; lower values measure TTL robustness under variable tool-call durations.

deadlock_unpins.description: Number of forced unpins used to recover schedulability; lower values penalize policies that rely on deadlock recovery.

completed_fraction.description: Fraction of programs completed by the scheduler run; higher values prevent latency gains from dropping or starving work.

delay_reduction_x.description: Average-completion speedup relative to the experiment baseline; higher values are the normalized headline benefit.

p90_delay_reduction_x.description: P90-completion speedup relative to the experiment baseline; higher values reward tail-latency improvements.

p95_delay_reduction_x.description: P95-completion speedup relative to the experiment baseline; higher values reward high-percentile latency improvements.

throughput_improvement_x.description: Throughput ratio relative to the experiment baseline; higher values reward machine-independent throughput gains.
